newsitem.title: BULGARIA: BULGARIA LEV ENDS UP ON PROFIT-TAKING, SEEN STABLE.
newsitem.headline: BULGARIA LEV ENDS UP ON PROFIT-TAKING, SEEN STABLE.

text.p: The Bulgarian lev advanced to
about 1,575-1,585 at close on Wednesday from the opening's
1,605-1,625 due to profit taking and was seen stable as a new
reformist government stepped in, dealers said.
"Banks and clients were unloading (foreign currency)
positions for profit-taking, hoping for lev stability to
continue under the new government. But trade was thin due to
low dollar demand," one dealer said.
The caretaker cabinet has stabilised the local currency at
between 1,500-1,600 per dollar since March.
Parliament appointed earlier on Wednesday a new cabinet led
by the head of pro-reform Union of Democratic Forces Ivan
Kostov who pledged to carry on the economic and financial
stabilisation policies of the interim government.
Rising yields on one- and four-week discount T-bills at
Wednesday's auctions also boosted foreign currency supply due
to expectations that a possible cut in the central bank main
interest rate from next week might be lower than expected.
The central bank has steadily pared its main rate from 18
percent monthly in March to 4.29 percent now.
The average yields to maturity on one- and four-week
discount T-bills sold on Wednesday rose to 0.49 and 3.82
percent, respectively, from 0.46 and 3.77 percent on Tuesday
and from 0.41 and 3.71 percent at Monday's auctions.
The central bank usually adjusts its main interest rate
each Thursday to the average effective monthly yields on those
types of T-bills auctioned daily from Friday through Thursday.
-- Sofia Newsroom, (++359-2) 911 88
